Recent notes

  • MX17 efficiency: where every track goes 2026-10-26Cosmic benchMicromegasEfficiency

    Every M3 track crossing a bench chamber followed to where it ends: det3 interior 91.2 % detected, 93.3 % found, 95.2 % of non-spark crossings; the rest is sparks, second particles, delta rays and the fit. All five chambers, interior and edge, 5 and 3 mm.

  • det3: where the lost tracks go, and what a better reconstruction could recover 2026-10-26Cosmic benchMicromegasEfficiencyReconstruction

    Each efficiency-loss category of det3 in the waveforms: sparks, second particles, δ-rays, saturated blobs, 2-strip seeds; the saturated-strip treatment in detail.

  • MX17 events that disagree with M3 2026-10-25Cosmic benchMicromegasReconstructionReference tracking

    Golden bench outliers classified event by event: M3 at fault ~0.8 % (bent tracks), second particles and delta rays 3 %, edge zone by band; competing-cluster and two-track follow-ups; det4/det7 head-on = known hardware; SPS open

  • One physical waveform model 2026-10-25Cosmic benchMicromegasReconstructionWaveform model

    One physics-set RC waveform model: det4 ladders back on timing v, chi2 halved; det3 unchanged; det7 X cost

  • Pogo-field short check 2026-10-25Cosmic benchMicromegasReadout

    A general check for M1 pogo-field pad shorts that is not fooled by charge sharing between neighbouring strips; applied to the June bench fleet.

  • det7 X pogo-field shorts 2026-10-25Cosmic benchMicromegasReadoutDet7

    Interactive map of the det7 X M1 pogo pad field (June bench, g_det7_long): which readout pads are shorted together, which strips each short joins, and why a rigid connector offset does not explain it.
